Subject: Questions on MSA redlines — regulatory fines / 3rd-party claims

Marcus — thanks for taking this. Legal at Acme flagged the liability cap & carve-out language in the MSA/Order Form. Two core asks: (1) confirm whether Redwood will accept that regulatory fines and penalties (GDPR / CCPA / PCI) are carved out of the liability cap, and (2) clarify treatment of third-party claims (e.g., fines / penalties paid to a regulator vs. amounts paid to a third party under a settlement).

We're hoping to avoid unlimited vendor liability broadly, but our legal team insists regulatory penalties potentially cannot be swept into a vendor cap. Can you confirm Redwood's position and any proposed redline?

Thanks — Amelia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Questions on MSA redlines — regulatory fines / 3rd-party claims

Amelia — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Legal (Laura, Rishi) and Contracts (Monica) to confirm redline options. High-level position from Sales/Contracting: Redwood's default is to keep a commercially reasonable liability cap for direct damages, but we understand customers want to exclude certain statutory fines. We have two negotiation paths that we've used recently — summarized below with pros/cons.

Option 1 — Narrow exclusion + sublimit (recommended by Redwood):
- Regulatory fines/penalties (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, PCI fines) are carved out of the general liability cap, BUT only to the extent they are finally adjudicated or imposed by a Governmental Authority against the Customer and directly resulting from Redwood's material breach or violation of law.
- Sublimit: Redwood proposes a sublimit for such excluded regulatory fines equal to the greater of (a) $3,000,000 or (b) the available proceeds of Redwood's relevant insurance policies (after application of deductible).
- Rationale: acknowledges customer concern about statutory fines while giving Redwood predictability and linkage to insurance where available.

Option 2 — Mutual carve-out with insurance-first approach (customer-favored):
- Regulatory fines and penalties are excluded from the cap and treated as direct liability (no sublimit).
- Parties agree to an insurance-first rule: Redwood's liability for such fines is limited to available insurance proceeds; any excess would be subject to further negotiation or carve-in.
- Rationale: gives Acme comfort but exposes Redwood to potentially uncapped liability if insurance shortfalls occur. Usually requires stronger indemnities and mutuality.

Third-party claims treatment (settlements with non-governmental third parties):
- Standard approach is that amounts paid to third parties under settlement that arise from Redwood's breach are treated as direct damages and fall under the general liability cap unless specifically carved out.
- If Acme wants these settlements carved out, we ask for: (a) a definition narrowing to settlements that are directly tied to Redwood's breach, and (b) right to defend/consent to settlement to avoid opportunistic claims.

Attached: suggested redline language drafts for both options (see Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx). Laura / Rishi / Monica — can you PTB (please take a look) and propose clean MSA / Order Form wording we can send to Acme?

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Team — reviewed and drafted a tighter clause that balances Acme's ask with Redwood's need for operational predictability. Below is a recommended insertion to the MSA (Order Form references to be mirrored):

"Regulatory Penalties; Third-Party Claims: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Agreement, amounts finally awarded or imposed by a Governmental Authority against Customer as civil or regulatory penalties, fines or statutory damages arising from Redwood's breach of its obligations under applicable Data Protection Laws (including but not limited to GDPR, CCPA) or payment card industry obligations (PCI DSS) shall be excluded from the liability cap set forth in Section X. Redwood's aggregate liability for such regulatory penalties shall not exceed the greater of (i) $3,000,000 and (ii) amounts actually recovered under Redwood's applicable insurance policies after the application of any deductible. For clarity, amounts paid by Customer to a third party in settlement of a claim (including amounts paid to a third party under a settlement with a Governmental Authority) will be governed by Section X (Limitation of Liability) unless the parties agree in writing that such settlement specifically arises from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence and that Redwood had notice and a reasonable opportunity to defend and consent to the settlement"

Key points:
- We explicitly tie the exclusion to fines "imposed by a Governmental Authority" to avoid runaway private-contractual claims being characterized as regulatory penalties.
- We include an explicit sublimit tied to insurance to avoid open-ended exposure.
- We preserve Redwood's right to defend and require notice/consent for third-party settlements.

If Sales wants to relax the sublimit number, speak with Finance first — the $3M floor is achievable but needs underwriting sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Marcus — appreciate the thoughtful approach but two points from Acme Legal: (1) Mutuality — Acme will not accept a carve-out that applies only to Redwood. If fines are excluded from Redwood's cap, the same exclusion should apply to Acme for any fines caused by Acme's actions (mutual carve-out); (2) Sublimit — $3M is a starting point but we view it as low for enterprise retail exposures; we'd consider a $10M sublimit or uncapped carve-out if Redwood will agree to enhanced security controls, incident response SLAs, and a warranty about PCI compliance testing.

We can live with the defense/consent language but want stronger obligations to cooperate post-incident (timely notifications, forensic reports, regulator liaison).

-David
David Keller
Deputy GC, Acme Retail

Thanks everyone — internal next steps and proposed counter for Acme: 

Action items (internal):
- Legal (Laura / Rishi): please finalize the draft clause, but update the sublimit proposal to $5,000,000 and include the following mandatory controls as conditions to a higher sublimit: SOC 2 Type II attestation (most recent), PCI Attestation of Compliance for relevant flows, and a documented incident response plan with defined SLA milestones (notification within 24 hours, triage report within 72 hours).
- Contracts (Monica): prepare a clean Order Form that references the finalized clause and the control requirements as schedule items.
- Sales (Marcus): offer Acme a compromise counter: (a) regulatory fines and penalties imposed by Government Authorities will be carved out of Redwood's general cap, but Redwood's liability for such fines will be capped at the greater of $5,000,000 or available insurance proceeds; (b) Redwood will extend mutual cooperation rights and will agree to mutual carve-out only if Acme agrees to symmetrical language (i.e., mutual carve-out where fines arise from the other party's breach).

External to Acme: draft to send tomorrow morning providing the proposed compromise and the attached redline. If Acme pushes for an uncapped carve-out we should escalate to Finance/CEO for approval — highlight to them the operational controls we've conditioned the higher sublimit on.

Marcus
